tasks.task: Write an SOP and a one-page checklist for one task

items.when: When a recurring task is done from memory and anyone in the role should be able to follow it
When the task has branches, to get a flowchart, who does what and the edge cases
When one person does the task alone and needs exact steps, fixes and who to call
When the draft is done, to test it for gaps and make a short deck to teach it
When the SOP uses office words, to rewrite it in the team's words and test it read aloud
When people skip the SOP, to make the task itself easier and use the words they use

tasks.task: Review old SOPs and guides and fix the gaps

items.when: When an old SOP exists and needs checking against how the work is done today
When there is a folder of SOPs, to find missing owners, stale pages and gaps
Each month, to flag stale or ownerless documents and draft the rewrites
When something went wrong, to turn the timeline into a safer procedure and tracked actions

tasks.task: Plan the SOP library and docs system

items.when: When know-how is scattered, to decide what to write down, where it lives and who keeps it fresh
When starting from nothing, to set up the system and write the first procedures with a check
When the team keeps its documents in Notion and wants to find and update them there

tasks.task: Map one process and find the delays

items.when: When one process needs mapping end to end with every wait, hand-off and redo marked
When you want a swim-lane map with cycle times and the one stage holding things up
When the steps are listed, to mark each as value or waste and name the worst
When there are records of late work, to map where it waits and back causes with data
When the map is drawn from a meeting room, to go and watch the work and its hand-offs

tasks.task: Design a leaner version of one process

items.when: When one process keeps causing delays or complaints and must be fixed, then written down
When the current map is agreed and a leaner flow and trial plan are needed
When the waste is clear but its cause is not, to find it and one change to try
When the fix could be small tweaks or a redesign, to compare two plans with cost and dates
Before a step or rule is cut, to see what else it quietly does
When the change is agreed, to tell the team what to do differently and from when

tasks.task: Find the constraint and plan capacity around it

items.when: When work piles up and you need the one step that caps output
When demand and what the team can make are known, to find the gap and a plan to close it
When the constraint is people, to see workload against hours and who is overloaded
When adding capacity costs money, to work out payback and risk on each option
When every step claims to be the problem, to find the limiting step and plan from it

tasks.task: Run the weekly operations review

items.when: Every week on the same day, to keep the review, the fixes and the watch list moving
When the week's numbers and notes are in and need one page of fixes with owners
Each week, to check last week's open actions and set the next agenda
When the owner wants a short written update in place of a meeting

tasks.task: Build a weekly or monthly KPI report

items.when: Before building, to pick the few measures the team can move week to week
When two people work a number out differently, to write one agreed definition
When the numbers exist but nobody reads them, to define them and write a plain weekly update
When the same report is needed each week and should be rerun, not rebuilt
When the owner also wants a trend, a forecast and a dashboard to share
Before the report goes out, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Run an operations health check

items.when: When recent weekly reviews exist, to see what keeps slipping before judging the whole
When the client can supply numbers, to score each function and show what data is missing
When growth has brought shortcuts, to see which changes watered down what customers liked
When the same problems return each quarter, to find the structure that keeps making them

tasks.task: Draw the roles chart and write role agreements

items.when: When nobody is sure who owns which task, or the business must see the roles before the people
When the structure itself is open, to get a plan, a spans check and who decides what
When roles need a scorecard, a meeting rhythm and 90-day goals around them

tasks.task: Audit the owner's week and plan what to hand over

items.when: When the owner is the bottleneck and wants to see doing, managing and building time
When there is no record of the week yet, to plan how to log it
When the owner cannot name what only they should do, to get a delegation plan
When daily operations run through the owner, to plan the handover task by task
When the owner now manages people, to set one-on-ones and the tasks that lift team output

tasks.task: Plan the handover of work only one person knows

items.when: When one person holds the know-how and is going on leave, leaving, or is too big a risk
When there is a recent real run of the task, to write the procedure and its exceptions
When the handover is days away, to write a note the next person can run from on day one

tasks.task: Build a recurring-tasks calendar

items.when: When stock counts, checks, renewals and reports are done from memory and get missed
When the calendar should live in a sheet, to get a clean file with the agreed fields
When reminders should fire on their own, to pick a simple set-up that holds up

tasks.task: Write the operations manual

items.when: When a second site, new manager or franchisee must run the business like the best site
Before the chapters, to put the service on one page of standards that can be checked
When the standards exist, to turn them into a job card per role and a missed-standard rule
When a chapter is drafted, to read it as a new manager and list what they would have to ask
When the manual describes ideals, to write the basics and try them in one place first

tasks.task: Prepare to open a second site

items.when: When the owner has decided to open another site or get ready to franchise
Before committing, to test whether the first site runs without the owner and list the gaps
When the best site must be written down as standards and a manual a stranger can follow
When the opening could be fast or staged, to compare two plans with money and dates

tasks.task: Test a franchise or partner-run model

items.when: Before offering a site to a partner, to see what they keep at forecast and at weaker sales
When the sums work, to put the terms for people who run the business on one page
When partners will need the manual and standards that come with the deal

tasks.task: Build a site visit scorecard

items.when: When an owner or area manager visits sites and needs a fair, repeatable way to score them
When there are no written standards to score against yet
When scores should be entered on a phone, logged and sent to the site manager

tasks.task: Write day-one documentation for a new team member

items.when: When the new person's first tasks have no written steps
When a start date is set, to plan pre-start checks, the first week and 30, 60 and 90 day goals
When the role needs a job card and a day-one trial sheet

tasks.task: Cut and fix recurring meetings, approvals and reports

items.when: When the calendar is full, to get a keep, simplify or drop call on each meeting and report
When a status meeting could be a written update, to sort each agenda item and the hours saved
When meetings end without owners, to turn the notes into actions with names and dates
Before a meeting or approval is dropped, to see what it quietly does for the team

tasks.task: Find why a problem keeps coming back

items.when: When the same problem returns, to build a chain of whys checked against facts
When a failure needs a no-blame review with the team and sized fixes
When the causes are known, to size a fix at each level with an owner, date and check
When each fix wears off, to look at the pattern over time and what feeds it

tasks.task: Set quarterly goals and a scorecard

items.when: When the quarter needs a few objectives, each with dated, numbered results
When goals need a scorecard, an accountability chart and a meeting rhythm to hold them
When goals are all end results, to pick the weekly measures that drive them

tasks.task: Decide what to automate and which tool to buy

items.when: Before automating, to get a verdict on whether the process should be, with risks and a fallback
When a task is worth automating, to pick the right Zapier or Make set-up
When tools are being compared, to score each against the client's needs
Before the team relies on it, to find double runs and missing approval steps

always.when: Before an SOP, manual chapter or review is shared, to catch typos and a task named two ways
When a review or report states numbers, to tie each to the client's own export or cut it

helpers.when: When the leaner process needs tools connected or a workflow built, not only designed
When the roles chart turns into a restructure with reporting lines and spans to redesign
When the KPI report needs messy exports joined, cleaned and analysed first
When a procedure covers safety, food hygiene or quality rules that differ by region
When the constraint is staffing and rotas, cover and headcount need planning
When SOPs must become a training programme with practice and sign-off

gaps: No library item builds a site visit scorecard with weighted standards, evidence notes and follow-up actions
No library item builds a recurring-tasks calendar of daily, weekly, monthly and yearly routines with owners
No library item writes role agreements for each position; the org chart items stop at structure
No library item runs a one-page weekly operations review from a small business's own numbers and notes
No library item sets pacing rules around a constraint for a kitchen, workshop or service team; the fits are factory-shaped
No library item writes a new site opening checklist with dates for fit-out, hiring, training and soft launch
No library item writes franchise manual chapters such as brand standards, audits and what a franchisee may change
No library item turns an SOP into a one-page checklist or job aid on its own
No library item checks a procedure against region-specific safety or food rules
No library item offers two or three clearly different SOP formats to test with the team
